text:
Noah Ostlund has stepped into a much bigger job in Buffalo this season. The 22-year-old Swede is playing almost 18 minutes a night, up from 14, and he's on the ice for 61% of the Sabres' power-play time after 15% last year. He has answered with 14 points in 24 games and a jump in his own chances, from 0.45 expected goals per 60 to 0.84.

For a forward picked 16th overall, the typical first full season produces 0.31 points a game. He's at 0.58. And there's more in it: the Sabres have scored 7 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him points. That usually swings back.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows how he plays: 67% of his shots come off the rush, he carries the puck in on 54% of his entries, and 20% of his setups go across the royal road, the pass that moves a goalie side to side. He scored in Sunday's win over Tampa Bay. A real middle-of-the-lineup player is taking shape.
